relationships.input: Minced rather than intact beef in the tested older-adult meal
relationships.biological_role: The tested texture change increased six-hour appearance of dietary phenylalanine in ten older men.
relationships.limitation: Single crossover with 135 g intrinsically labelled beef. Total plasma EAA concentrations and muscle protein synthesis did not differ detectably. Not a universal meat, protein or neurotransmitter prescription; earlier no-selected-SOP wording records the prior assessment.

relationships.input: Pair non-haem iron-containing meals with an ascorbic-acid source
relationships.biological_role: Ascorbic acid can counter phytate- and polyphenol-related inhibition and improve non-haem iron absorption at the meal level. Iron is a required cofactor for tyrosine hydroxylase.
relationships.limitation: Evidence supports improved non-haem iron absorption at the meal level; it does not establish improved iron status or any change in dopamine biology or function.

relationships.input: Use validated phytate-reducing preparation methods for high-phytate cereals
relationships.biological_role: Phytase treatment can reduce phytate inhibition and improve non-haem iron absorption from some cereal matrices. Iron is a required cofactor for tyrosine hydroxylase.
relationships.limitation: Improved absorption was matrix-dependent and did not consistently translate into better long-term iron status; no dopamine-related outcome was measured.

relationships.input: Short-term selective dietary-fat restriction in adults with obesity under controlled conditions
relationships.biological_role: Five days of selective isocaloric fat restriction reduced striatal D2/D3 receptor binding potential and food-cue activity in adults with obesity; selective carbohydrate restriction did not produce the same change.
relationships.limitation: Evidence comes from 17 adults with obesity in a short inpatient experiment; reduced binding potential does not by itself distinguish receptor change from greater endogenous dopamine occupancy.

relationships.input: Short-term very-low-calorie dieting in adults with obesity
relationships.biological_role: About ten days of very-low-calorie dieting reduced substantia-nigra D2/D3 receptor binding potential in women with obesity, and regional changes tracked reductions in leptin.
relationships.limitation: The uncontrolled study involved 15 women with obesity and cannot establish whether the imaging change reflects altered receptor availability or endogenous dopamine occupancy.

relationships.input: Experimental DHA–UMP co-supplementation
relationships.biological_role: DHA plus uridine monophosphate (UMP) increased gerbil hippocampal spine density more than DHA alone in the tested exposure.
relationships.limitation: Four weeks, choline present in all diets, small animal-level sample. UMP alone was not significant for spine density. This is an experimental combination, not a human supplementation recommendation.

relationships.input: Experimental spermidine supplementation in ageing
relationships.biological_role: Spermidine feeding prevented ageing-related enlargement of presynaptic release sites in fruit flies.
relationships.limitation: It did not restore reduced synapse numbers. Human wheat-germ-extract memory results were null; neither those results nor the fly study establish human structural benefit.

relationships.input: Active-period feeding under obesogenic exposure (experimental)
relationships.biological_role: A defined active-period feeding schedule changed regional spine maintenance in mice exposed to an obesogenic diet.
relationships.limitation: Four-week mouse protocol after prolonged high-fat/high-sucrose exposure. Regionally opposite structural responses; no human eating-window target or general healthy-adult benefit established.

relationships.input: Experimental magnesium-L-threonate exposure
relationships.biological_role: The tested formulation changed presynaptic structural markers in rats.
relationships.limitation: Puncta are markers, not ultrastructurally verified contact counts. Formulation- and region-specific animal evidence does not establish that ordinary magnesium foods increase human synapses or improve ADHD.

relationships.input: Tested fibre/fruit-rich mixed meal versus the high-fat/high-carbohydrate comparison
relationships.biological_role: The meal comparison measured different acute mononuclear NF-kB DNA-binding responses.
relationships.limitation: Small parallel-group acute comparison; multiple ingredients and macronutrients differed. No isolated fibre, fruit or constituent effect; LAL/LBP are not direct proof of gut leakage, portal origin, LPS bioactivity or brain benefit. CRP and TNF-alpha did not change.

relationships.input: Tested fibre/fruit-rich mixed meal versus the high-fat/high-carbohydrate comparison
relationships.biological_role: The meal comparison measured different acute plasma endotoxin/LBP responses.
relationships.limitation: Small parallel-group acute comparison; multiple ingredients and macronutrients differed. No isolated fibre, fruit or constituent effect; LAL/LBP are not direct proof of gut leakage, portal origin, LPS bioactivity or brain benefit. CRP and TNF-alpha did not change.

relationships.input: Myrosinase-completed broccoli sprout homogenate
relationships.biological_role: Three daily doses of broccoli sprouts, blended with water and daikon sprouts and held at 37°C so myrosinase could finish forming sulforaphane, increased phase II enzyme RNA in nasal cells of healthy adults. The authors read that shared pattern as Nrf2-linked induction. They did not measure Nrf2 protein or its movement into the nucleus.
relationships.limitation: This is three days of that homogenate in healthy adults and nasal enzyme RNA, not brain Nrf2, an ordinary broccoli serving, or the four-week sprout-extract capsules that did not raise lung target-gene expression in COPD.

relationships.input: Limit unnecessary cumulative heat exposure when retaining creatine in pork products
relationships.biological_role: Controlled pork-loin and cooked-ham experiments found greater creatine-to-creatinine conversion with higher heat exposure, especially at the product surface.
relationships.limitation: Evidence is limited to processed pork matrices and does not establish higher creatine intake or cerebral target engagement.

relationships.input: Consider creatine monohydrate only in defined low-intake or high-demand contexts
relationships.biological_role: Human reviews indicate that supplementation can raise cerebral total creatine or phosphocreatine modestly and variably, while a small crossover trial during sleep deprivation found concurrent changes in cerebral high-energy phosphates and cognitive performance.
relationships.limitation: Effective dosing and responder characteristics remain uncertain, and cognitive trials do not consistently measure cerebral target engagement.

relationships.input: Experimental carnitine/carbohydrate loading protocol
relationships.biological_role: The tested 24-week exposure increased muscle carnitine and changed exercise-dependent fuel handling.
relationships.limitation: Lipid use is partly inferred from glycogen sparing; CPT transport flux was not directly measured. Large carbohydrate co-exposure and extracted formulation are not meat/dairy effects or a routine dietary recommendation.

relationships.input: Four-day ketogenic liquid formula in the studied healthy-adult experiment
relationships.biological_role: The defined formula raised tracer/model-estimated cerebral acetoacetate metabolism.
relationships.limitation: Small short-term nonrandomised study; PET metabolic rates are tracer/model estimates, not direct neuronal oxidation measurements. Combined total ketone energy contribution was estimated separately. No ADHD efficacy or endorsement of routine ketogenic dieting.

relationships.input: Include dietary fat with provitamin-A vegetables
relationships.biological_role: Dietary fat supports absorption of vegetable provitamin-A carotenoids upstream of the vitamin A–retinoid biology recorded for this PM.
relationships.limitation: Measured carotenoid absorption, not vitamin A conversion, intestinal retinoic-acid delivery or improved tight-junction function. Applies to the tested vegetable meal; do not generalise to every fat-soluble compound, impose the study fat dose, or promise reduced permeability.

relationships.input: Tested fibre/fruit-rich mixed meal versus the high-fat/high-carbohydrate comparison
relationships.biological_role: The meal comparison measured different acute plasma endotoxin/LBP responses.
relationships.limitation: Small parallel-group acute comparison; multiple ingredients and macronutrients differed. No isolated fibre, fruit or constituent effect; LAL/LBP are not direct proof of gut leakage, portal origin, LPS bioactivity or brain benefit. CRP and TNF-alpha did not change.

relationships.input: Wholemeal rye bread in place of the tested refined wheat bread
relationships.biological_role: The tested replacement slowed early model-derived glucose appearance.
relationships.limitation: The result applies to the tested breads and does not identify one responsible nutrient.

relationships.input: Fish before rice in the studied meal sequence
relationships.biological_role: Fish first delayed gastric emptying, an upstream control of carbohydrate delivery.
relationships.limitation: An acute meal result; no claim that protein alone accounts for the effect.

relationships.input: The tested high-slowly-digestible-starch breakfast in place of extruded cereal
relationships.biological_role: The high-slowly-digestible-starch product redistributed glucose appearance from earlier to later in the morning.
relationships.limitation: Measured in 12 tracer participants after specific breakfasts; no universal product, dose or longer-term outcome claim.

relationships.input: The studied whey preload before a carbohydrate meal
relationships.biological_role: Whey given before the studied meal delayed scintigraphic gastric emptying and stimulated insulin and gut hormones.
relationships.limitation: Eight adults with diet-controlled type 2 diabetes; 55 g whey 30 min before the meal, additional energy, acute results. No universal preload prescription or direct requirement.

relationships.input: The tested semolina pasta matrix in place of semolina bread or couscous
relationships.biological_role: The pasta matrix retained starch within larger particles and a protein network during the assessed digestion steps.
relationships.limitation: Separate human and simulated-digestion experiments; appearance slowing is inferred, not quantified. The result does not apply to every pasta or processing method.

relationships.input: Cooling and reheating the tested chickpea pasta
relationships.biological_role: Cooling and reheating increased measured resistant starch in this pasta, reducing the readily digestible fraction as a plausible entry-pathway change.
relationships.limitation: Twelve healthy adults; 24 h at 4 °C and the tested reheating method. Glucose entry was not measured and digestible carbohydrate was not re-matched after processing.

relationships.input: The tested beta-glucan addition to a polenta meal
relationships.biological_role: The studied 5 g beta-glucan addition redistributed exogenous glucose appearance from the first two hours to later in the six-hour period.
relationships.limitation: Twelve overweight adults; no lower overall appearing quantity and no universal fibre effect. Viscosity is a proposed explanation, not a measured mediator.

relationships.input: The tested guar–chickpea flour flatbread blend
relationships.biological_role: The 4% guar and 15% chickpea flour formulation modestly reduced four-hour exogenous glucose appearance in the tested flatbread.
relationships.limitation: The primary half-absorption-time endpoint did not change significantly; larger liver-production and disposal changes also occurred. No isolated guar effect or general fibre requirement.

relationships.input: Isomaltulose instead of sucrose in the studied sugar-load comparison
relationships.biological_role: The tested substitution slowed estimated oral-glucose appearance under the study conditions.
relationships.limitation: Eleven adults with type 2 diabetes under a clamp; not an instruction to add sugar. A separate 12-week trial did not show an HbA1c advantage.

relationships.input: Vinegar with the studied starchy meal
relationships.biological_role: The matched-meal trial supports a possible delay in gastric delivery from its lower paracetamol-marker response.
relationships.limitation: Indirect marker in ten healthy volunteers, no appearance flux. Further delay occurred in diabetic gastroparesis and may be disadvantageous; do not apply this practice to that context.

relationships.input: Less-processed whole-grain food package (two-week trial)
relationships.biological_role: In adults with type 2 diabetes, the tested less-processed whole-grain package reduced daily glucose standard deviation and mean amplitude of glycaemic excursions (MAGE) versus a nutrient-matched finely processed package over two weeks.
relationships.limitation: A food package, not an isolated grain or fibre effect; unmasked foods, short duration. Concealed randomisation, blinded CGM, initial masked analysis and intention-to-treat models support appraisal.

relationships.input: Early eating with front-loaded calories (six-day trial)
relationships.biological_role: In a small prediabetes crossover, the tested early, front-loaded eating schedule reduced mean amplitude of glycaemic excursions (MAGE) over six days versus later calorie distribution; mean glucose and several other variability/range measures were inconclusive.
relationships.limitation: Small sample, no washout; timing, eating-window length and calorie distribution cannot be separated.

relationships.input: Diet-induced weight reduction when excess adiposity is relevant
relationships.biological_role: The assessed programme improved measured insulin sensitivity in adults with obesity.
relationships.limitation: This is conditional on the studied metabolic context, not a general recommendation to lose weight.

relationships.input: Conditional oral arginine supplementation in the tested type-2-diabetes protocol
relationships.biological_role: The studied 9 g/day exposure improved clamp-measured glucose disposal in a small clinical comparison.
relationships.limitation: Incomplete normalisation; small selected clinical population. cGMP change does not isolate causal NO mediation. The 9 g/day supplement protocol is not equivalent to arginine-containing food.

relationships.input: Aligned sleep–wake and meal scheduling
relationships.biological_role: The experiment establishes that combined behavioural misalignment disrupts daily cortisol timing.
relationships.limitation: Restoring every abnormal rhythm and the separate contribution of each cue were not tested.

relationships.input: EPA+DHA supplementation (studied combined formulation)
relationships.biological_role: The higher-dose combined exposure changed RMSSD and total power in the trial.
relationships.limitation: Small elevated-triglyceride sample; no separated EPA/DHA necessity or routine benefit claim.

relationships.input: Food-related mindfulness training
relationships.biological_role: The tested programme reduced reported stress-eating tendencies and cravings.
relationships.limitation: Self-report and pseudo-randomized allocation; neural mediation and real-world intake remain unproven.
